title: experimental-lit-bisect-notes-arjun-2024-12
content:
Topline: a very rough working log for a lit-driven bisect approach. Trying to isolate why certain prompts show a quality drop when we enable 4-bit quant + aggressive KV eviction + batching. Mix of paper summaries, quick hypotheses, and an experiment plan. Notes to self style — messy.

Why this doc: stash quick paper takeaways + map to concrete microbench experiments we can run on staging. Want to be able to say: degradation mostly due to X (kv eviction pattern) vs Y (quantization rounding) vs Z (cross-batch KV contamination). Use small isolated tests that change one axis at a time.

Papers/blogs skimmed (short summaries):
- "KV-cache sparsity and eviction policies" (internal notes + related academic bits)
  - main idea: eviction heuristics that consider token salience reduce regret. But most evals assume full-precision. Question: does lowbit quantized KV materially alter salience ordering? If yes, eviction picks wrong keys.
  - takeaway: need a probe that measures rank-shift of attention-weighted keys when we quantize representations.

- "Low-bit quantization and distributional drift" (blog + paper)
  - observed: 4-bit quant can introduce subtle bias in dot products that increases with sequence length.
  - actionable: add unit test computing pairwise dot product error between float32 and quantized KV rows over typical prefixes.

- "Batching and cross-request cache interference" (conference talk screencaps)
  - summary: dynamic batching that coalesces requests can cause KV caches to see overlapping context from different conversations if the eviction/namespace is buggy; even well-scoped caches show timing effects.
  - note: our runtime namespaces look correct but eager reuse could still mix up partial cache writes if there's a race.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction ordering mismatch under quantization: quantized keys change nearest-neighbor ordering -> wrong prefix hits -> hallucinations / quality drop.
2) Batch-induced partial-kv exposure: when batching is on and we pre-allocate KV shards, some in-flight writes lead to stale/partial keys being used for subsequent tokens.
3) Quantization rounding amplification over long prefixes: small dot-error accumulates and changes top-k attention.
4) Tuning interplay (temp, top_p) interacts with any of the above and amplifies observable QA score drops.

Short experiments to run (minimal, orthogonal):
- Experiment A: Pairwise dot-error probe
  - dataset: 1000 random prefix-token pairs sampled from production anonymized prompts (low-PII subset)
  - compute dot(float32) vs dot(quantized) for KV rows at multiple prefix lengths (64, 256, 1024)
  - metric: fraction where sign/top-k flips vs baseline
  - expected: if >1% top-k flips at 1024 then quantization is suspicious

- Experiment B: Eviction sensitivity test
  - deterministic tiny model snapshot (2-3 layers emulation if needed) or a small Llama-ish toy
  - simulate a cache with LRU vs salience-based eviction while toggling quantization
  - feed adversarial prefixes that create similar keys (near duplicates)
  - metric: downstream answer divergence (exact-match or BLEU) when eviction differs

- Experiment C: Batch race microbench
  - instrument the serving-runtime to add a debug flag that forces a 5ms sleep between KV compute and commit (simulated partial write)
  - run high qps small-batch workload and look for request IDs that saw partial prefix hits
  - metric: incidence of malformed outputs / mismatch between expected and actual KV length

- Experiment D: End-to-end QA regression A/B
  - controlled: baseline fp16/no-eviction, test: 4-bit+aggressive-evict+batching
  - prompt set: 500 curated QA prompts where we previously saw regressions
  - metrics: EM, F1, perplexity, and a qualitative failure-tag set (halluc, truncated, format-broke)

Quick notes on instrumentation we need:
- expose an internal flag to dump raw KV vectors pre/post-quantization for a given request id
- add a lightweight probe that computes top-10 neighbor indices for a probe key across full cache and compares float vs quantized indices
- telemetry: count of top-k flips per model/sequence-length/quant-profile

Immediate TODOs (next 2 days):
- Lina: add probe endpoints to serving-runtime debug branch (link: PR #421) — minimal perf impact. (assigned)
- Owen: run dot-error probe on the 4-bit runner using sample 1k prefixes from the staging corpus. Dump CSV with flip rates. (assigned)
- Me: set up small toy eviction sim (python) and mock quantization function to iterate on eviction policy tests.
- Create a shared Confluence page summarizing results with flags for rollback if quantization shows >2% top-k flips at long context.

Open questions / things to watch for:
- Are we comparing quantization at weight level vs activation level? Most low-bit libs quantize weights only; we quantize activations for KV too — need to be explicit in test matrix.
- Some users report degradation only for retrieval-heavy prompts. Could be interaction between RAG score and quantization noise.
- Timing: how often do partial writes happen in practice vs our injected test? If rare, may be more an edge-case but still important for worst-case SLAs.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiments orthogonal: one axis at a time. If we toggle both batch and quant together we won't bisect.
- Use synthetic near-duplicate keys to stress eviction; real data too but synthetic gives repeatability.
- Watch out for measurement noise: run each micro-experiment 10x and report median + 90th pct.

Scratch snippets / commands (rough):
- sample prefixes: python tools/sample_prefixes.py --source staging --n 1000 --minlen 32
- dot probe: python infra/dot_probe.py --model fp32.ckpt --quant 4bit.cfg --out dots.csv
- simulate eviction: python dev/evict_sim.py --policy lru,salience --quantize on,off --runs 50

Links / references I want to revisit:
- low-bit quant blog (internal link): CONFLU-QUANT-2024
- attention-sparsity preprint: arXiv:2409.xxxx (save pdf to drive later)
- internal slack thread: #kv-cache-quirks (thread ts 1700000000)

Log:
- 2024-12-05: initial reading and hypothesis list. Created probe skeleton.
- 2024-12-08: PR for debug kv-dump created (PR #421) — Lina
- 2024-12-12: ran initial dot-error on small sample, saw ~0.6% top-k flips at 256, 1.8% at 1024 (preliminary) — need more runs.
- 2025-01-09: Owen posted expanded CSV; 1024 flip rate median 1.9%, 90th pct 3.4% on heavy-retrieval prompts.

If we confirm quantization flips are the dominant factor (>2% correlates with EM drop >4 pts), mitigation paths:
- switch KV to fp16 but keep other tensors 4-bit (selective dequant)
- adopt an eviction policy that falls back to fp16 similarity scoring for candidate comparison
- increase quantization fidelity for long-context model shards only (per-shard profiles)

Final quick thought: this doc should live until we have clear attribution. When experiments finish, move a cleaned summary to Confluence and mark this as archived. For now: noisy, messy, exactly what I need to iterate.
